title: Complications, risks and diagnostic significance of endomyocardial biopsies for the diagnosis of cardiomyopathies in children and adolescents
summary:
Background: Endomyocardial biopsy is an established procedure in adults for diagnosing heart muscle diseases and monitoring rejection reactions in heart transplant recipients. In children and adolescents, it remains controversial due to associated risks and complications.

The study investigates how frequently complications occur during endomyocardial biopsies in children and adolescents, what risk factors exist for the occurrence of complications, what the diagnostic value of endomyocardial biopsy is in this age group, and to what extent biopsy results influence further therapy.
A retrospective analysis of all endomyocardial biopsies in patients at LMU University Hospital Munich in the Department of Pediatric Cardiology and Pediatric Intensive Care Medicine during the period from 2015 to 2025 is conducted, including collection of patient data, indications, complications, histological findings, and discharge letters.
conditions: Failure and rejection of transplanted organs and tissues
